endorsements.quote: Rather, the role bridges the CMO’s clinical accountability and the CIO’s technical infrastructure authority, with specific responsibility for (1) AI model certification and recertification, (2) local calibration auditing and equity reporting, and (3) institutional AI governance policy—functions currently unhoused in either the CMO or CIO role.

The road map’s 2035 pivot requires a parallel legal innovation: a framework for collaborative medical agency that assigns shared accountability across the human clinician, the institution’s CAIO, and the AI system’s certified governance record.

First, a decision record log —analogous to a flight data recorder—could capture the AI system’s inputs, confidence scores, and flagged uncertainties for every consequential clinical recommendation, creating an auditable governance trail for adverse event review.

Third, a graduated autonomy protocol —mirroring aviation’s phased certification of autopilot authority at different flight stages—could specify the conditions under which agentic AI is permitted to act without real-time human confirmation, with those conditions contractually tied to demonstrated calibration performance.

First, an equity audit mandate for the CAIO requires annual recalibration of local SLMs against nationally representative benchmarks, with mandatory public reporting of disaggregated performance metrics stratified by age, race, sex, and socioeconomic status.
Third, a public transparency layer requiring institutions to publish SLM performance statistics across demographic strata would create accountability pressure independent of regulatory enforcement.
An SLM that surfaces its reasoning—linking each diagnostic flag to a specific guideline citation—functions simultaneously as a safety guardrail and a real-time teaching tool [ 21 ].

unlisted_practices: Standardize dual-process AI architectures in which a locally deployed small language model verifies LLM outputs and flags low-confidence claims for mandatory clinician review.
Establish formal minimum verification requirements for AI-assisted clinical decision support, analogous to postmarket surveillance for medical devices.
Designate a formally credentialed chief AI officer with accountability equivalent to the chief medical officer.
Revise medical licensing, accreditation, and malpractice liability frameworks to recognize AI-assisted decisions as collaborative clinical output.
Integrate futures literacy and human-AI teaming competencies into medical curricula.
Establish a cross-institutional calibration exchange with standardized data use agreements so health systems can share calibration data.
Require minimum training data diversity for locally deployed small language models.
Name the CAIO as a coinsured party in institutional malpractice instruments for AI-assisted decisions.
Extend AI semantic transparency into patient-facing plain-language explanations and give the CAIO a patient education function.
Offer CAIO-as-a-service models through regional networks for small or resource-limited health systems.
Review the road map's technological assumptions at each pivot point through an adaptive checkpoint mechanism.
Validate the dual-process architecture and trust thresholds prospectively through multi-institutional studies and multistakeholder Delphi consensus.
